es: Reconocer expresiones de probabilidad (definitely, highly likely, probably, unlikely, a slim chance, no chance), ordenarlas por fuerza y ligarlas al nivel de riesgo de un aviso.

teaching.en: The forecast says it will definitely snow on the mountain tonight.
teaching.es: El pronóstico dice que sin duda nevará en la montaña esta noche.
teaching.explanationEs: Will definitely + verbo: certeza casi total; el adverbio va después de will.
segments: The forecast says it will definitely
snow on the mountain tonight.
teaching.audioText: The forecast says it will definitely snow on the mountain tonight.

teaching.en: Heavy rain is highly likely on Saturday, so the warning is serious.
teaching.es: La lluvia fuerte es muy probable el sábado, así que el aviso es serio.
teaching.explanationEs: Highly likely: probabilidad alta. Likely es adjetivo: is likely to + verbo.
segments: Heavy rain is highly likely on
Saturday, so the warning is serious.
teaching.audioText: Heavy rain is highly likely on Saturday, so the warning is serious.

teaching.en: It will probably be cloudy, but it probably won't rain.
teaching.es: Probablemente estará nublado, pero probablemente no lloverá.
teaching.explanationEs: Will probably, pero probably won't: con la negación el adverbio va antes de won't.
segments: It will probably be cloudy,
but it probably won't rain.
teaching.audioText: It will probably be cloudy, but it probably won't rain.

teaching.en: Ice is unlikely before noon, but it is still a hazard after dark.
teaching.es: Es poco probable que haya hielo antes del mediodía, pero sigue siendo un peligro al anochecer.
teaching.explanationEs: Unlikely = poco probable. Hazard nombra el peligro; la probabilidad es otra cosa.
segments: Ice is unlikely before noon, but it
is still a hazard after dark.
teaching.audioText: Ice is unlikely before noon, but it is still a hazard after dark.

teaching.en: There is a slim chance of sunshine, so take a raincoat.
teaching.es: Hay una posibilidad escasa de sol, así que lleva un impermeable.
teaching.explanationEs: A slim chance: baja pero no nula. No chance significa imposible.
segments: There is a slim chance of
sunshine, so take a raincoat.
teaching.audioText: There is a slim chance of sunshine, so take a raincoat.

prompt.es: Elige la frase con la probabilidad más alta.

choices.text: The road might be closed.
The road is unlikely to be closed.
The road will definitely be closed.

feedback.es: Will definitely deja casi sin duda que ocurrirá; might lo deja abierto y unlikely lo vuelve poco probable.

hint.es: Busca la forma que casi no deja duda de que ocurrirá.

prompt.es: Completa: «Es muy probable que nieve esta noche.»

feedback.es: Highly likely + to + verbo expresa una probabilidad alta; likely es el adjetivo que lo permite.

hint.es: Es el adjetivo que significa «probable» y se escribe antes de to.

origin.text: Snow is highly ___ to fall tonight.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Probablemente no nevará en el valle.»

answer.text: It probably won't snow in the valley

feedback.es: Con la negación, probably va antes de won't: probably won't + verbo.

hint.es: El adverbio va antes de la forma negativa won't.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase del parte con su grado de probabilidad.

The wind will probably drop tonight.

There is no chance of rain tonight.

feedback.es: Definitely marca casi certeza, probably una probabilidad media-alta, unlikely poca y no chance la excluye.

choices.text: Low temperatures are certain.
Rain after lunch is certain.

feedback.es: A slim chance indica una probabilidad baja pero no nula.

There is no chance of leaving the harbour today.

choices.text: The flight will be cancelled.
The fog will clear at six.
The departure will be delayed.

feedback.es: Probably leave a little late anuncia un retraso; la cancelación es unlikely y las noticias a las seis son seguras.

feedback.es: Con la negación, probably se coloca antes de won't.

choices.text: The train might be late.
The train will definitely be late.
The train can't be late.

feedback.es: Might deja la posibilidad abierta; definitely la vuelve casi segura y can't la excluye.

choices.text: The shop is certainly still open.
She believes the shop is already shut.
The shop opens again later tonight.

feedback.es: Hazard nombra la fuente de peligro; aquí, el hielo en la carretera.

origin.text: Ice is a ___ for drivers.

title.es: En el caso poco probable de

es: Formular avisos de riesgo con in the unlikely event (of/that), the odds are, there's a slim chance y the worst-case scenario, eligiendo la estructura que sigue a cada expresión.

teaching.en: In the unlikely event of a fire, leave the building by the stairs.
teaching.es: En el caso poco probable de un incendio, salga del edificio por las escaleras.
teaching.explanationEs: In the unlikely event of + nombre, + instrucción: el aviso formal de seguridad.
segments: In the unlikely event of a fire,
leave the building by the stairs.
teaching.audioText: In the unlikely event of a fire, leave the building by the stairs.

teaching.en: In the unlikely event that the ferry is cancelled, you will receive a full refund.
teaching.es: En el caso poco probable de que se cancele el transbordador, recibirá un reembolso completo.
teaching.explanationEs: In the unlikely event that + oración completa; el resultado va con will o con un imperativo.
segments: In the unlikely event that the ferry is
cancelled, you will receive a full refund.
teaching.audioText: In the unlikely event that the ferry is cancelled, you will receive a full refund.

teaching.en: The odds are that the trail will be open by noon.
teaching.es: Lo más probable es que el sendero esté abierto al mediodía.
teaching.explanationEs: The odds are (that) + oración: probabilidad alta. Pese al español, no lleva subjuntivo.
segments: The odds are that the trail
will be open by noon.
teaching.audioText: The odds are that the trail will be open by noon.

teaching.en: There's a slim chance that the guide will need to evacuate the camp.
teaching.es: Hay una posibilidad escasa de que el guía tenga que evacuar el campamento.
teaching.explanationEs: There's a slim chance (that) + oración: probabilidad baja.
segments: There's a slim chance that the guide
will need to evacuate the camp.
teaching.audioText: There's a slim chance that the guide will need to evacuate the camp.

teaching.en: The worst-case scenario is that the path floods and we turn back.
teaching.es: En el peor de los casos, el camino se inunda y damos la vuelta.
teaching.explanationEs: The worst-case scenario is (that) + oración: nombra lo peor que podría pasar.
segments: The worst-case scenario is that the
path floods and we turn back.
teaching.audioText: The worst-case scenario is that the path floods and we turn back.

prompt.es: Completa: «En el caso poco probable de que se cancele el vuelo, llame a este número.»

feedback.es: Tras event, una oración completa se introduce con that; of se reserva para un nombre.

origin.text: In the unlikely event ___ the flight is cancelled, call this number.

prompt.es: Elige el aviso correcto para un corte de luz.

choices.text: In the unlikely event of a power cut, use the torch.

hint.es: Fíjate en lo que sigue a event of: solo un nombre, sin verbo conjugado.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Hay una posibilidad escasa de que la puerta siga cerrada.»

feedback.es: There's a slim chance that + oración con will expresa una probabilidad baja sobre el futuro.

hint.es: Empieza con There's y deja la oración completa tras that.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada aviso en inglés con su traducción.

origin.text: The ___ are that she will arrive on time.

choices.text: Take the lift to the ground floor.
Go to the closest way out on foot.
Wait in the room until morning.

feedback.es: El aviso pide caminar hasta la salida más cercana, no usar el ascensor y esperar instrucciones de la tripulación.

choices.text: There's a slim chance that the market will be busy on Saturday.
There's no chance that the market will be busy on Saturday.
The odds are that the market will be busy on Saturday.

A room at a hotel.
A seat on the morning train.

feedback.es: El aviso promete que, si cancelan el tren, un taxi los llevará a casa sin coste.

feedback.es: Refund es el reembolso que se promete en caso de cancelación.

es: Comprender un parte de montaña: localizar el peligro, su grado de certeza (will, are expected, may), el momento y la urgencia de la acción recomendada.

teaching.en: Gusts of sixty kilometres an hour are expected above the ridge.
teaching.es: Se esperan ráfagas de sesenta kilómetros por hora por encima de la cresta.
teaching.explanationEs: Are expected: el parte anuncia el peligro con voz pasiva; busca el fenómeno, la cifra y el lugar.
segments: Gusts of sixty kilometres an hour
are expected above the ridge.
teaching.audioText: Gusts of sixty kilometres an hour are expected above the ridge.

teaching.en: Visibility will drop sharply in cloud after noon.
teaching.es: La visibilidad caerá bruscamente entre nubes después del mediodía.
teaching.explanationEs: Will drop: previsto casi con seguridad. Sharply indica que el cambio será rápido.
segments: Visibility will drop sharply
in cloud after noon.
teaching.audioText: Visibility will drop sharply in cloud after noon.

teaching.en: Thunderstorms are possible by mid-afternoon, so hikers should be off the summit early.
teaching.es: Son posibles tormentas eléctricas a media tarde, así que los excursionistas deberían bajar pronto de la cima.
teaching.explanationEs: Are possible: no es seguro. Should be off: consejo con urgencia media.
segments: Thunderstorms are possible by mid-afternoon, so hikers
should be off the summit early.
teaching.audioText: Thunderstorms are possible by mid-afternoon, so hikers should be off the summit early.

teaching.en: Temperatures will fall below freezing, so the descent may be slippery.
teaching.es: Las temperaturas bajarán de cero, así que el descenso podría ser resbaladizo.
teaching.explanationEs: Below freezing = por debajo de cero (sin of). May marca un riesgo posible.
segments: Temperatures will fall below freezing, so
the descent may be slippery.
teaching.audioText: Temperatures will fall below freezing, so the descent may be slippery.

teaching.en: Treat this as a serious alert and turn back at once if the wind increases.
teaching.es: Tómelo como una alerta seria y dé la vuelta de inmediato si aumenta el viento.
teaching.explanationEs: Serious y at once elevan la urgencia: hay que actuar ya, no más tarde.
segments: Treat this as a serious alert and turn
back at once if the wind increases.
teaching.audioText: Treat this as a serious alert and turn back at once if the wind increases.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué peligro anuncia el parte.

choices.text: Heavy snow in the valley.
Strong wind on the high ground.
Fog over the lake.

feedback.es: Gusts son ráfagas de viento y el parte las sitúa sobre la cresta, es decir, en la zona alta.

hint.es: Piensa qué son las ráfagas y en qué zona se esperan.

prompt.es: Lee el parte y elige cuánta certeza tiene sobre las tormentas.

choices.text: They are certain to arrive before two.
They are impossible today.
They are possible, but not certain.

feedback.es: Are possible indica que pueden ocurrir, pero no lo afirma; will habría marcado certeza.

hint.es: Observa si el parte usa will o una expresión de posibilidad.

origin.text: Thunderstorms are possible after two o'clock, so hikers should be off the summit early.

prompt.es: Completa: «La visibilidad caerá bruscamente entre nubes.»

feedback.es: Visibility es lo lejos que se ve; en un parte suele caer cuando hay nubes o niebla.

hint.es: Es el sustantivo que mide cuánto se puede ver a lo lejos.

origin.text: ___ will drop sharply in cloud.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada señal del parte con lo que indica.

pairs: Gusts are expected above the ridge.
Thunderstorms may develop after two.
Leave the summit at once if the sky turns black.
Conditions will change gradually over the week.

feedback.es: Are expected señala algo previsto, may algo posible, at once urgencia alta y gradually un cambio lento.

pairs: Gusts are expected above the ridge.
Thunderstorms may develop after two.
Leave the summit at once if the sky turns black.
Conditions will change gradually over the week.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué se recomienda a quien sigue en la montaña.

choices.text: To begin going down before dark.
To stay on the ridge all night.
To wait for the ice to melt.

feedback.es: El parte advierte de un descenso resbaladizo y recomienda empezar a bajar antes de que oscurezca.

origin.audio: Afternoon update. Temperatures will fall below freezing tonight, so the descent from the ridge may be slippery. Anyone still on the mountain should start down before dark.

prompt.es: Completa: «Tómelo como una alerta seria.»

feedback.es: Serious alert señala un aviso de urgencia alta.

origin.text: Take this as a serious ___.

prompt.es: Según el parte, ¿qué es seguro que ocurrirá?

choices.text: Thunderstorms will begin after four.
A cold front will reach the ridge.
The paths will be frozen.

feedback.es: Will marca lo seguro: el frente frío llegará. Las tormentas son solo posibles y la noche será templada.

origin.text: Mountain forecast: A cold front will reach the ridge by midday. Gusts of up to eighty kilometres an hour are expected on the high ground. Thunderstorms are possible after four. The night will stay mild.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué urgencia tiene el aviso para los barcos.

choices.text: They can go out after lunch.
They should wait until the evening.
They must come back immediately.

feedback.es: At once marca urgencia alta: el puerto cierra a mediodía y los barcos deben volver ya.

origin.audio: Coastal alert. A strong wind is expected from nine, and the waves will be high. The harbour will close at noon, so all boats should return at once.

feedback.es: Below freezing significa por debajo de cero grados.

prompt.es: ¿Qué urgencia tiene la nota del guía?

Everyone must turn back at once.
The guide sees no risk at all.

feedback.es: La nota habla de visibilidad posiblemente mala, pero dice que nadie necesita cancelar: precaución sin urgencia alta.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué se aconseja para esta noche.

choices.text: Climbers should leave before the storm.
Nobody should start a new climb.
The wind is nothing to worry about.

feedback.es: El aviso anuncia tormentas y viento fuerte, y aconseja no empezar ninguna escalada nueva.

prompt.es: Completa: «Según el parte, habrá ráfagas fuertes esta noche.»

feedback.es: El bulletin es el parte oficial del tiempo en el que se anuncian las ráfagas.

origin.text: According to the ___, there will be strong gusts tonight.

es: Redactar avisos y consejos de seguridad con unless, provided that / as long as, in case y had better, usando presente tras la conjunción y verbo base tras had better.

teaching.en: Do not start the climb unless the weather is clear.
teaching.es: No empieces la subida a menos que el tiempo esté despejado.
teaching.explanationEs: Unless ya significa «si no»: no se le añade otra negación.
segments: Do not start the climb
unless the weather is clear.
teaching.audioText: Do not start the climb unless the weather is clear.

teaching.en: You may camp here provided that you leave no rubbish.
teaching.es: Puedes acampar aquí siempre que no dejes basura.
teaching.explanationEs: Provided that / as long as + presente: condición necesaria; no se usa will detrás.
segments: You may camp here provided
that you leave no rubbish.
teaching.audioText: You may camp here provided that you leave no rubbish.

teaching.en: Take a torch in case the path is dark.
teaching.es: Lleva una linterna por si el camino está oscuro.
teaching.explanationEs: In case + presente: te preparas antes de que pase; no equivale a if.
segments: Take a torch in case
the path is dark.
teaching.audioText: Take a torch in case the path is dark.

teaching.en: You had better turn back if the route is icy.
teaching.es: Más vale que des la vuelta si la ruta está helada.
teaching.explanationEs: Had better + verbo base, sin to: consejo fuerte con una consecuencia implícita.
segments: You had better turn back
if the route is icy.
teaching.audioText: You had better turn back if the route is icy.

teaching.en: You will be fine as long as you carry a waterproof jacket.
teaching.es: Estarás bien siempre que lleves una chaqueta impermeable.
teaching.explanationEs: As long as equivale a provided that en el habla diaria; condición necesaria.
segments: You will be fine as long
as you carry a waterproof jacket.
teaching.audioText: You will be fine as long as you carry a waterproof jacket.

teaching.en: It is sensible to rest in the shelter if the storm arrives.
teaching.es: Es sensato descansar en el refugio si llega la tormenta.
teaching.explanationEs: It is sensible to + verbo: un consejo razonable, más suave que had better.
segments: It is sensible to rest in
the shelter if the storm arrives.
teaching.audioText: It is sensible to rest in the shelter if the storm arrives.

prompt.es: Elige el aviso que solo permite subir con buena visibilidad.

choices.text: Don't climb unless the visibility isn't good.
Don't climb provided that the visibility is bad.
Don't climb unless the visibility is good.

feedback.es: Unless equivale a «si no» y lleva la condición en positivo; con otra negación el aviso se contradice.

hint.es: Unless ya significa «si no»: no añadas otra negación.

prompt.es: Completa: «Puedes entrar siempre que lleves casco.»

feedback.es: Provided that y as long as expresan la condición necesaria, «siempre que»; detrás va el presente.

hint.es: Busca un conector con el sentido de «siempre que».

answer.text: Take some water in case it is hot

feedback.es: In case + presente expresa prevención: llevas el agua antes de que haga calor.

hint.es: In case va antes de la oración que describe la posibilidad.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada aviso con la idea que expresa.

pairs: Bring a map in case the signal fails.
You can swim as long as a lifeguard is here.
Don't swim unless a lifeguard is here.
You had better leave now.

feedback.es: In case previene, as long as fija una condición, unless marca una excepción a la prohibición y had better aconseja con fuerza.

pairs: Bring a map in case the signal fails.
You can swim as long as a lifeguard is here.
Don't swim unless a lifeguard is here.
You had better leave now.

Ask the guard before lighting it.
Never light a fire on the campsite.

prompt.es: Completa: «Más vale que lleves un abrigo; hará frío.»

feedback.es: Had better + verbo base da un consejo fuerte y el adjetivo better es parte fija de la estructura.

origin.text: You had ___ take a coat; it will be cold.

prompt.es: Elige el aviso que refleja la regla de la playa.

choices.text: Don't swim unless the red flag isn't down.
Don't swim unless the red flag is down.
Swim in case the red flag is down.

feedback.es: La regla admite nadar solo si la bandera roja está abajo; unless la expresa sin negación adicional.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué debe hacer la persona para conservar su cama.

choices.text: Book one week before by post.
Bring some sheets from home.
Arrive before six and phone the cabin.

title.en: Risk briefing for a mountain trip
title.es: Charla de riesgos para una excursión

es: Presentar en una charla breve los riesgos de una excursión (peligro, probabilidad, consecuencia y medida de prevención) y deducir las causas de un incidente con must have, might have y can't have.

teaching.en: This briefing has three parts: the hazard, the risk and the measure we take.
teaching.es: Esta charla tiene tres partes: el peligro, el riesgo y la medida que tomamos.
teaching.explanationEs: Una charla de riesgos sigue un orden fijo: peligro, riesgo (probabilidad) y medida.
segments: This briefing has three parts: the hazard,
the risk and the measure we take.
teaching.audioText: This briefing has three parts: the hazard, the risk and the measure we take.

teaching.en: Ice is likely on the ridge, and the consequence could be a serious injury.
teaching.es: Es probable que haya hielo en la cresta, y la consecuencia podría ser una lesión grave.
teaching.explanationEs: Después de la probabilidad se nombra la consecuencia: could be + lo que podría pasar.
segments: Ice is likely on the ridge, and
the consequence could be a serious injury.
teaching.audioText: Ice is likely on the ridge, and the consequence could be a serious injury.

teaching.en: To prevent a fall, all participants must check their equipment.
teaching.es: Para evitar una caída, todos los participantes deben revisar su equipo.
teaching.explanationEs: To prevent + nombre abre la medida; must marca la obligación.
segments: To prevent a fall, all
participants must check their equipment.
teaching.audioText: To prevent a fall, all participants must check their equipment.

teaching.en: The path is wet, so the incident must have happened after the rain.
teaching.es: El camino está mojado, así que el incidente debe de haber ocurrido después de la lluvia.
teaching.explanationEs: Must have + participio: deducción casi segura sobre el pasado, a partir de una prueba.
segments: The path is wet, so the incident
must have happened after the rain.
teaching.audioText: The path is wet, so the incident must have happened after the rain.

teaching.en: There is no evidence of wind damage, so the cause can't have been the storm.
teaching.es: No hay indicios de daños por el viento, así que la causa no puede haber sido la tormenta.
teaching.explanationEs: Can't have + participio: deducción negativa casi segura.
segments: There is no evidence of wind damage, so
the cause can't have been the storm.
teaching.audioText: There is no evidence of wind damage, so the cause can't have been the storm.

teaching.en: The incident might have started with a missed turn.
teaching.es: El incidente podría haber empezado con un giro que no se tomó.
teaching.explanationEs: Might have + participio: posibilidad sobre el pasado, sin seguridad.
segments: The incident might have started
with a missed turn.
teaching.audioText: The incident might have started with a missed turn.

prompt.es: Escribe el guion de una charla de riesgos para una excursión.

answer.text: Good morning, everyone. This briefing has three parts: the hazards, the risks and the measures we take. The first hazard is ice on the ridge. It is likely after such a cold night, and the consequence could be a serious injury. To prevent a fall, all participants must wear strong boots, and you had better walk slowly. The second hazard is the river. In the unlikely event that the water rises, we will turn back at once. There is a slim chance of thunderstorms after two o'clock, so we will be off the ridge by one. Nobody should cross the river unless the guide says it is safe. Please carry a torch in case we come down after dark. Finally, check your equipment now, so that nothing breaks on the way. Are there any questions?
accepted: Good morning, everyone. This briefing has three parts: the hazards, the risks and the measures we take. The first hazard is ice on the ridge. It is likely after such a cold night, and the consequence could be a serious injury. To prevent a fall, all participants must wear strong boots, and you had better walk slowly. The second hazard is the river. In the unlikely event that the water rises, we will turn back at once. There is a slim chance of thunderstorms after two o'clock, so we will be off the ridge by one. Nobody should cross the river unless the guide says it is safe. Please carry a torch in case we come down after dark. Finally, check your equipment now, so that nothing breaks on the way. Are there any questions?

Hello, team. Today I want to explain two risks. The main hazard is the wind on the high ground. Strong gusts are very likely, and the consequence could be a fall or another injury. To prevent it, we will stay on the marked route, and you had better hold your hats. The other hazard is the cold. The odds are that it will freeze tonight, so everybody must bring a warm coat, provided that there is space in the bag. In case anyone feels dizzy, tell me at once. Unless the forecast improves, we will not climb the summit. Does everyone understand?

feedback.es: Una charla clara nombra cada peligro, dice cuán probable es, avisa de la consecuencia y cierra con una medida de prevención (to prevent, unless, in case, so that, had better).
